notes: Both coders called the document delegates. Main disagreements: (1) policy_type between neighbouring types for discussion-framework and faculty-use prompts (P63/P109, P69/P124, P70/P44, P102/P59, P121/P59), resolved by re-reading the sentence against each type's definition, keeping UNCOVERED where neither type covered the whole rule (shared instructor-student responsibility; unit review-and-report). (2) Modality (informs vs should vs must): imperatives for 'each' syllabus and institutional 'will' commitments set to must; questions and benefit statements to informs. (3) Splitting: coder B split compound sentences (privacy guidance; faculty review vs honor-code bodies may set rules; two clauses of 'GAI may not be appropriate'); resolved to one rule per unit. B's units that repeat the same sentence or rule (P85 'department/unit' frame, 'students already using GAI', second PD clause, 'Adapted from' byline) were dropped; 11 B-only units kept after checking the text (mostly discussion questions and one scope statement); 2 A-only units kept (consequences clause, CAT tools). Each A unit is matched to its B counterpart; extra units created by splitting A units are not counted in only_B unless B had them.
